With his many attacks in the mountains, Buitrago claimed 78 points, 16 more than Van Aert. Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) is third in the standings (36 points).
There are no categorised climbs on today’s route."],"stage":21,"_id":"377536858485d3be3ac42ec532d1b7890ffd5b806c9d0d2f6b5ee2a07fcda867","_bind":"publication_en-2026-21","_origin":"news-2026-21","_updatedAt":1789307820359,"_parent":"stage-2026:8bb74c198b26df28aad6a71f95413b41e60ab24297655aa1f08b2fa1aba9c744","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:polka-dot-jersey-132","model":"news"},{"stage":21,"id":71510,"updatedAt":"2026-09-13T16:54:42+02:00","updatedBy":"bvittek","text":["Enric Mas, 31, La Vuelta 2026

Zoetemelk went on to win the Tour de France in 1980, and Rominger won La Vuelta in 1993 and 1994 again before adding the Giro d’Italia to his record in 1995. winner of stage 8 in Xeraco, Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) hopes to be in the mix today: “It’s always special. For a start, it’s really great to finish a Grand Tour, especially when you’ve had some success in it. I’m really pleased to have won. I wanted to stay there to celebrate with my mates right up until the very last moment! And yes, today is a bit of a mixed bag. Let’s just say it’s going to be selective and tough. But we’ll do our very best to try and secure a good result. I think Van Aert will be able to attack. It will be his second victory in a Grand Tour standings, after the points classification of the Tour de France 2022.
After his breakaway yesterday, Van Aert has 326 points, 87 more than his Visma-Lease a Bike teammate Matthew Brennan. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) completes the top 3 with 171 points.
There are 50 points up for grabs today: 20 at the intermediate sprint and 30 at the finish."],"pinned":false,"updatedAt":"2026-09-13T15:53:45+02:00","updatedBy":"bvittek","type":"liv","stage":21,"slug":"green-jersey-133","highlight":false,"createdAt":"2026-09-13T15:53:45+02:00","createdBy":"bvittek","picto":"liv_green_jersey","stageType":"PLN","locale":"en","id":71328,"title":"Green jersey","year":2026,"_id":"e3b8ac59e13f4bd7f59e59b7a2761caee2dcdb3969006c1103f455a2fd48e532","_bind":"publication_en-2026-21","_origin":"news-2026-21","_updatedAt":1789307625329,"_parent":"stage-2026:8bb74c198b26df28aad6a71f95413b41e60ab24297655aa1f08b2fa1aba9c744","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:green-jersey-133","model":"news"},{"createdAt":"2026-09-13T18:04:33+02:00","createdBy":"bvittek","picto":"liv_interview","locale":"en","highlight":false,"stageType":"PLN","year":2026,"publicationAt":"2026-09-13T18:04:33+02:00","title":"Romele: "I’m gonna suffer like the first days and will do my best"","type":"liv","updatedBy":"bvittek","updatedAt":"2026-09-13T18:04:33+02:00","slug":"romele-im-gonna-suffer-like-the-first-days-and-will-do-my-best","id":71678,"stage":21,"text":["Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) discovered himself at La Vuelta 26 and aims fora final strong performance today:
"Yes, actually, I was thinking [I may not finish] in the two easiest stages of this Vuelta, the first two stages of the third week. I don’t know what to say; it was maybe a virus, maybe not good recovery… Thanks to the doctor of the team, we managed, and here we are; last stage of the Vuelta, it’s a beautiful day. I spent 21 days in a super team, really good feelings, and we see today. It’s the last stage, I’m gonna suffer like the first days and will do my best.
We can say it’s a new start, maybe a new chapter of y career. We’ll see what the end of the season will be like with this shape. Hopefully I can manage to do something good in the Italian classics, maybe Paris-Tours… We don’t know. First of all, a good recovery after the Vuelta, and then we’re gonna see.""],"pinned":false,"_id":"55f109844ae0ddf09eaba2678ee2051e43530fa696e443bd41ee40ebe2bcc789","_bind":"publication_en-2026-21","_origin":"news-2026-21","_updatedAt":1789315474071,"_parent":"stage-2026:8bb74c198b26df28aad6a71f95413b41e60ab24297655aa1f08b2fa1aba9c744","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:romele-im-gonna-suffer-like-the-first-days-and-will-do-my-best","model":"news"},{"url":"https://x.com/lavuelta/status/2099147417392148555","createdBy":"ganz","updatedBy":"ganz","pinned":false,"type":"twitter","createdAt":"2026-09-13T16:46:45+02:00","socialContentLangs":[{"createdAt":"2026-09-13T16:46:45+02:00","createdBy":"ganz","title":"Départ réel","updatedBy":"ganz","updatedAt":"2026-09-13T16:46:45+02:00","locale":"fr"},{"updatedBy":"ganz","title":"Real start","createdBy":"ganz","createdAt":"2026-09-13T16:46:45+02:00","locale":"en","updatedAt":"2026-09-13T16:46:45+02:00"},{"title":"Salida lanzada","locale":"es","createdBy":"ganz","createdAt":"2026-09-13T16:46:45+02:00","updatedBy":"ganz","updatedAt":"2026-09-13T16:46:45+02:00"}],"onlyDataTab":false,"publicationAt":"2026-09-13T16:33:00+02:00","stage":{"date":"2026-09-13T00:00:00+02:00","stage":21,"podiumDisplayMode":"instantpodium","length":112,"type":"PLN","timezone":"Europe/Madrid","isCancelled":false,"lengthDisplay":112,"showGroups":true},"id":1951,"highlight":true,"onlyClubTab":false,"updatedAt":"2026-09-13T16:46:45+02:00","_id":"d8d99dde0dae76f8bedb3dad71cd6328b71ed958c0ba46ea326e7dbb8347ea6e","_bind":"publication_en-2026-21","_origin":"socialContent-2026-21","_updatedAt":1789310806043,"_parent":"stage-2026:8bb74c198b26df28aad6a71f95413b41e60ab24297655aa1f08b2fa1aba9c744","_key":"_id","_virtual":"social:d8d99dde0dae76f8bedb3dad71cd6328b71ed958c0ba46ea326e7dbb8347ea6e","model":"socialContent","title":"Real start","locale":"en"},{"onlyDataTab":false,"imageLangs":[{"locale":"fr","legend":"13/09/2026 - their final La Vuelta stage: "Joy and emotion"","pinned":false,"stageType":"PLN","publicationAt":"2026-09-13T16:42:10+02:00","text":["Jesús Herrada (Burgos-Burpellet-BH): "Well, rather than sadness, it’s the emotion of looking back on all those years and all those moments: the good ones, the bad ones… It’s not sadness, it’s joy and emotion at all those moments that are coming to an end today. But anyway, this stage is over and a new one is beginning. There aren’t enough words to express my gratitude for the year I’ve had with [Burgos-Burpellet-BH]. They’ve treated me absolutely brilliantly, and honestly, I couldn’t have had a better final year. The ideal ending would have been a stage win. Today is our last chance. We know it’s very difficult, we’ve tried and we’ll definitely try again. So let’s enjoy it and give it our all."
Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious): "I’m excited. Up until now I’ve been more relaxed, more calm, holding back those emotions a little and focusing more on the day-to-day, on the race. But anyway, today I’m feeling more excited. Well, I’ve got to fight it out right to the end, in my own style, and not let this chance slip by. I’m raring to go. I know there’s a lot of accumulated fatigue, and today could also be a good chance to prove myself right to the end, to give it my all. And one of us – either me or Pau [Miquel] – I hope we’ll be in the fight for the stage win. I’ll carry on a bit further and we’ll say our goodbyes at Il Lombardia."
Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility): "I think it will be very difficult, but I will definitely try to win today, and the team is there to support me. I think, if we would race from km 0 and from a breakaway, it would be a stage that would really suit me well, from a break. But I think, from the peloton, it will be more difficult for me. But I will do everything I can. I’ve always loved being in La Vuelta, and Spain in general, I’ve spent a big part of my career in Spain, so I want to say thank you to all the people of Spain for having me and being friendly my whole career. Spain has a special place in my heart, it’s my favourite country for racing, but also for training."
David De La Cruz (Pinarello-Q36.5): "No, no [I’m not sad]. I certainly have a mix of emotions, obviously. Today is my last race as a professional cyclist; I’m finishing the season here at La Vuelta a España, my final season. Lots of emotions, but sadness is certainly not one of them. I’m finishing La Vuelta with injuries, but also with fond memories, not just of this Vuelta, but also of the other twelve I’ve taken part in. Gosh, I’m absolutely delighted and so grateful to have been able to live this dream. Yesterday, too, on the final climb, the Alguacil, I had the chance to savour the moment and feel the warmth of the crowds, which was something special and incredibly moving. So, I’m leaving with a full heart and feeling incredibly grateful."

Madrid is the venue that has crowned the final winners on most occasions (55), ahead of Bilbao (13), San Sebastián (6), Santiago de Compostela (3), and then Miranda de Ebro, Salamanca and Jerez de la Frontera (1 each).
Granada was a stage town already in the first La Vuelta (1935), and it hosted the Gran Salida in 2005 and 2008. The iconic Alhambra was visited by La Vuelta in 1974, 1975 and 2005. The last stage winner in Granada is Adam Yates two years ago.
Granada has hosted many other cycling events, including Spain’s national road championships last year. Ivan Romeo won the men elite ITT.

their final La Vuelta stage: "Joy and emotion"","pinned":false,"stageType":"PLN","publicationAt":"2026-09-13T16:42:10+02:00","text":["Jesús Herrada (Burgos-Burpellet-BH): "Well, rather than sadness, it’s the emotion of looking back on all those years and all those moments: the good ones, the bad ones… It’s not sadness, it’s joy and emotion at all those moments that are coming to an end today. But anyway, this stage is over and a new one is beginning. There aren’t enough words to express my gratitude for the year I’ve had with [Burgos-Burpellet-BH]. They’ve treated me absolutely brilliantly, and honestly, I couldn’t have had a better final year. The ideal ending would have been a stage win. Today is our last chance. We know it’s very difficult, we’ve tried and we’ll definitely try again. So let’s enjoy it and give it our all."
Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious): "I’m excited. Up until now I’ve been more relaxed, more calm, holding back those emotions a little and focusing more on the day-to-day, on the race. But anyway, today I’m feeling more excited. Well, I’ve got to fight it out right to the end, in my own style, and not let this chance slip by. I’m raring to go. I know there’s a lot of accumulated fatigue, and today could also be a good chance to prove myself right to the end, to give it my all. And one of us – either me or Pau [Miquel] – I hope we’ll be in the fight for the stage win. I’ll carry on a bit further and we’ll say our goodbyes at Il Lombardia."
Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility): "I think it will be very difficult, but I will definitely try to win today, and the team is there to support me. I think, if we would race from km 0 and from a breakaway, it would be a stage that would really suit me well, from a break. But I think, from the peloton, it will be more difficult for me. But I will do everything I can. I’ve always loved being in La Vuelta, and Spain in general, I’ve spent a big part of my career in Spain, so I want to say thank you to all the people of Spain for having me and being friendly my whole career. Spain has a special place in my heart, it’s my favourite country for racing, but also for training."
David De La Cruz (Pinarello-Q36.5): "No, no [I’m not sad]. I certainly have a mix of emotions, obviously. Today is my last race as a professional cyclist; I’m finishing the season here at La Vuelta a España, my final season. Lots of emotions, but sadness is certainly not one of them. I’m finishing La Vuelta with injuries, but also with fond memories, not just of this Vuelta, but also of the other twelve I’ve taken part in. Gosh, I’m absolutely delighted and so grateful to have been able to live this dream. Yesterday, too, on the final climb, the Alguacil, I had the chance to savour the moment and feel the warmth of the crowds, which was something special and incredibly moving. So, I’m leaving with a full heart and feeling incredibly grateful."
Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) spoke yesterday: "I have to say that [this Vuelta] is a special one. We've won seven stages with the team already. Hopefully we can add one more this weekend, but it's a really nice way of ending my career. I still had a good feeling on the bike, so I didn't have the feeling I couldn't support the team anymore. I did my job in the last few weeks, so I'm really grateful to be part of this team and to end it like this. And for sure, I always love this race. I had some good results myself as well. It's always really nice to race in Spain and I have good memories about it.""],"locale":"en","stage":21,"id":71484,"slug":"the-retirees-words-ahead-of-their-final-la-vuelta-stage-joy-and-emotion","type":"liv","updatedAt":"2026-09-13T16:42:10+02:00","updatedBy":"bvittek","_id":"695374c8206544ba88be628cea41781bdfc5553f4d2a7022d5b9af8d7bbfd36b","_bind":"publication_en-2026-21","_origin":"news-2026-21","_updatedAt":1789310531129,"_parent":"stage-2026:8bb74c198b26df28aad6a71f95413b41e60ab24297655aa1f08b2fa1aba9c744","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:the-retirees-words-ahead-of-their-final-la-vuelta-stage-joy-and-emotion","model":"news"},{"highlight":false,"socialContentLangs":[{"locale":"fr","updatedAt":"2026-09-13T17:09:49+02:00","title":"Marcel Camprubi (Pinarello-Q36.5)","createdBy":"ganz","createdAt":"2026-09-13T17:09:49+02:00","updatedBy":"ganz"},{"updatedAt":"2026-09-13T17:09:49+02:00","title":"Marcel Camprubi (Pinarello-Q36.5)","locale":"en","createdBy":"ganz","createdAt":"2026-09-13T17:09:49+02:00","updatedBy":"ganz"},{"updatedAt":"2026-09-13T17:09:49+02:00","title":"Marcel Camprubi (Pinarello-Q36.5)","locale":"es","createdAt":"2026-09-13T17:09:49+02:00","createdBy":"ganz","updatedBy":"ganz"}],"publicationAt":"2026-09-13T17:00:00+02:00","stage":{"type":"PLN","length":112,"timezone":"Europe/Madrid","showGroups":true,"date":"2026-09-13T00:00:00+02:00","stage":21,"lengthDisplay":112,"podiumDisplayMode":"instantpodium","isCancelled":false},"updatedAt":"2026-09-13T17:09:49+02:00","embedCode":"

Enric Mas (Movistar) is set to become the 64th different overall winner of La Vuelta. their final La Vuelta stage: "Joy and emotion"","pinned":false,"stageType":"PLN","publicationAt":"2026-09-13T16:42:10+02:00","text":["Jesús Herrada (Burgos-Burpellet-BH): "Well, rather than sadness, They’ve treated me absolutely brilliantly, and honestly, I couldn’t have had a better final year. The ideal ending would have been a stage win. Today is our last chance. We know it’s very difficult, we’ve tried and we’ll definitely try again. So let’s enjoy it and give it our all."
Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious): "I’m excited. Up until now I’ve been more relaxed, more calm, holding back those emotions a little and focusing more on the day-to-day, on the race. But anyway, today I’m feeling more excited. Well, I’ve got to fight it out right to the end, in my own style, and not let this chance slip by. I’m raring to go. I know there’s a lot of accumulated fatigue, and today could also be a good chance to prove myself right to the end, to give it my all. And one of us – either me or Pau [Miquel] – I hope we’ll be in the fight for the stage win. I’ll carry on a bit further and we’ll say our goodbyes at Il Lombardia."
Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility): "I think it will be very difficult, but I will definitely try to win today, and the team is there to support me. I think, if we would race from km 0 and from a breakaway, it would be a stage that would really suit me well, from a break. But I think, from the peloton, it will be more difficult for me. But I will do everything I can. I’ve always loved being in La Vuelta, and Spain in general, I’ve spent a big part of my career in Spain, so I want to say thank you to all the people of Spain for having me and being friendly my whole career. Spain has a special place in my heart, it’s my favourite country for racing, but also for training."
David De La Cruz (Pinarello-Q36.5): "No, no [I’m not sad]. I certainly have a mix of emotions, obviously. Today is my last race as a professional cyclist; I’m finishing the season here at La Vuelta a España, my final season. Lots of emotions, but sadness is certainly not one of them. I’m finishing La Vuelta with injuries, but also with fond memories, not just of this Vuelta, but also of the other twelve I’ve taken part in. Gosh, I’m absolutely delighted and so grateful to have been able to live this dream. Yesterday, too, on the final climb, the Alguacil, I had the chance to savour the moment and feel the warmth of the crowds, which was something special and incredibly moving. So, I’m leaving with a full heart and feeling incredibly grateful."

Primoz Roglic is set to stand on the podium of La Vuelta for the 6th time: winner in 2019, 2020, 2021, and 2024; second in 2026; third in 2023. He matches Roberto Heras' record. Only Alejandro Valverde has more La Vuelta GC top 3 results: 7. Behind them, Enric Mas is up to 5, like Pedro Delgado and Luis Ocaña.
Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) is set to be the first Austrian podium finisher in La Vuelta. their final La Vuelta stage: "Joy and emotion"","pinned":false,"stageType":"PLN","publicationAt":"2026-09-13T16:42:10+02:00","text":["Jesús Herrada (Burgos-Burpellet-BH): "Well, rather than sadness, it’s the emotion of looking back on all those years and all those moments: the good ones, the bad ones… It’s not sadness, it’s joy and emotion at all those moments that are coming to an end today. But anyway, this stage is over and a new one is beginning. There aren’t enough words to express my gratitude for the year I’ve had with [Burgos-Burpellet-BH]. They’ve treated me absolutely brilliantly, and honestly, I couldn’t have had a better final year. The ideal ending would have been a stage win. Today is our last chance. We know it’s very difficult, we’ve tried and we’ll definitely try again. So let’s enjoy it and give it our all."
Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious): "I’m excited. Up until now I’ve been more relaxed, more calm, holding back those emotions a little and focusing more on the day-to-day, on the race. But anyway, today I’m feeling more excited. Well, I’ve got to fight it out right to the end, in my own style, and not let this chance slip by. I’m raring to go. I know there’s a lot of accumulated fatigue, and today could also be a good chance to prove myself right to the end, to give it my all. And one of us – either me or Pau [Miquel] – I hope we’ll be in the fight for the stage win. I’ll carry on a bit further and we’ll say our goodbyes at Il Lombardia."
Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility): "I think it will be very difficult, but I will definitely try to win today, and the team is there to support me. I think, if we would race from km 0 and from a breakaway, it would be a stage that would really suit me well, from a break. But I think, from the peloton, it will be more difficult for me. But I will do everything I can. I’ve always loved being in La Vuelta, and Spain in general, I’ve spent a big part of my career in Spain, so I want to say thank you to all the people of Spain for having me and being friendly my whole career. Spain has a special place in my heart, it’s my favourite country for racing, but also for training."
David De La Cruz (Pinarello-Q36.5): "No, no [I’m not sad]. I certainly have a mix of emotions, obviously. Today is my last race as a professional cyclist; I’m finishing the season here at La Vuelta a España, my final season. Lots of emotions, but sadness is certainly not one of them. I’m finishing La Vuelta with injuries, but also with fond memories, not just of this Vuelta, but also of the other twelve I’ve taken part in. Gosh, I’m absolutely delighted and so grateful to have been able to live this dream. Yesterday, too, on the final climb, the Alguacil, I had the chance to savour the moment and feel the warmth of the crowds, which was something special and incredibly moving. So, I’m leaving with a full heart and feeling incredibly grateful."
Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) spoke yesterday: "I have to say that [this Vuelta] is a special one. We've won seven stages with the team already.
